extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent attorneys/agents and applicants handling inventorship corrections
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for correcting inventorship in U.S. patent applications (nonprovisional and provisional) under 37 CFR 1.48 and related rules, including when to use petitions, required statements, fees, assignee consents, and effects on continuing/benefit claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of conflicting papers when no executed declaration filed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an executed declaration is never submitted and the application papers are in conflict as to the inventorship, each party identified as an inventor on filing will be considered to have been named as part of the inventive entity. See 37 CFR 1.41(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the baseline rule when no executed oath/declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 has been filed; later submissions may change inventorship only as provided in the rules (e.g., 37 CFR 1.48(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 37 CFR 1.47 to supply an oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.47 is available to meet the requirement for an oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63, for example where originally named inventors differ from a later-added inventor who refuses to cooperate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an oath/declaration under 1.63 cannot be obtained, an oath/declaration under 1.47(a) may be supplied, but the required 37 CFR 1.48(a)(2) statement must still be supplied by the added inventor or waived by petition under 37 CFR 1.183. Petitions under 1.47 apply only to an original oath/declaration and not to reexecution of another oath/declaration by an earlier inventor; use 1.183 to request waiver of reexecution (1.64) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: When petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is appropriate for reexecution waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.183 should be considered requesting waiver of the requirement of 37 CFR 1.64 that each actual inventor execute the oath or declaration, particularly where assignee consent is given to the requested correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent assignee consent, petitions under 1.183 will be evaluated as to whether the nonsigning inventor was actually given the opportunity to reexecute, or whether the nonsigning inventor could not be reached. If processing fee not submitted, the request will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees required for requests and petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where waiver under 37 CFR 1.183 is requested in relation to a requirement under 37 CFR 1.48(a), a processing fee under 37 CFR 1.48(a) and a petition fee under 37 CFR 1.183 are required. If multiple petitions/requests are presented separate fees are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a similar error has occurred in more than one application a separate processing fee must be submitted in each application. Failure to submit or authorize required fees will result in dismissal of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written consent of assignee for 37 CFR 1.48(a) requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The written consent of every existing assignee of the original named inventors must be submitted for requests under 37 CFR 1.48(a). 37 CFR 1.48(a) does not limit assignees to those recorded in USPTO records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no assignee exists requester should affirmatively state that fact. The individual signing for an assignee must state authority to act; in absence of such statement, consent will be accepted if signed by appropriate official whose title is of record. Assignee must establish ownership per 37 CFR 3.73 and MPEP §324.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship overlap requirement for claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 120 permits a continuing application to claim the benefit of the filing date of a copending, previously filed, parent application provided there is inventorship overlap between the continuing application and the parent application. If the inventive entity of a continuing application includes an inventor named in the parent application, the overlap required by 35 U.S.C. 120 is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlap need not be present on the date the continuing application is filed, nor when the parent application issues or becomes abandoned. However, loss of overlap (e.g., due to deletions) can prevent claiming benefit; examiners should consider intervening references if benefit is lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prior oath/declaration copies when filing continuations/divisionals
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a continuation or divisional under 37 CFR 1.53(b), a copy of an oath or declaration from the prior application can only be used where inventors are to be deleted, but not where inventors are to be added. Where inventors are to be added, a newly executed oath or declaration must be submitted. See 37 CFR 1.63(d)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a continuation/divisional is filed purporting to add an inventor using a copy of the prior oath, the inventorship of the prior application will be retained in the continuing application and addition is not permitted. Recommended practice: file continuation/divisional with a newly executed oath/declaration when adding an inventor to eliminate need for a 37 CFR 1.48 request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic consideration of 1.48 requests in CPAs (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a continued prosecution application (CPA) filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d), a request under 37 CFR 1.48(a) or (c) to add an inventor to a parent application that was not acted on will be automatically considered in the CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: effective July 14, 2003, CPA practice has been eliminated as to utility and plant applications. For design applications, CPA refiling under 1.53(d)(4) is possible when only deletions are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.78 copendency and filing fee requirement for benefit claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a continuing application to correct inventorship, 37 CFR 1.78 requires that for purposes of claiming benefit of the prior application the prior application must have had the filing fee (or basic filing fee per post-2005 practice) paid within the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.53(f) to establish copendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective July 1, 2005, the basic filing fee (not just the former processing and retention fee) must be paid during pendency of a nonprovisional to permit benefit to be claimed under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) in a subsequent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if continuation/divisional purports to add inventor using prior oath copy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a continuation or divisional is filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b)(1) using a copy of the oath/declaration from the prior application purporting to add an inventor, the inventorship of the prior application will be retained in the continuing application and addition is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The retained inventorship must then be corrected by filing a request under 37 CFR 1.48(a) in the continuation/divisional stating the error was without deceptive intention. Filing a continuation/divisional with a new oath is recommended to avoid the 1.48 process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential rejections when correction request denied
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request to correct inventorship is denied, a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or (g) must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denial may result in loss of inventorship overlap between parent and continuing applications and inability to claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 — examiners must consider intervening references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding to Office of Petitions when request accompanied by 1.183 petition
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary examiner may not decide a 1.48 request if it is accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 requesting waiver of one of the requirements explicitly set forth in 37 CFR 1.48(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, the request and petition should be forwarded to the Office of Petitions for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-paragraph deficiencies: Statement of facts must state lack of deceptive intent
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement of facts by an inventor or inventors to be added or deleted must explicitly state that the inventorship error occurred without deceptive intent on his or her part or be construed to so state (form paragraph 2.13a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the statement cannot be so construed, the request is deficient. Use appropriate follow-on form paragraphs (2.13b-2.13g) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-paragraph deficiencies: Submission of new oath/declaration required
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration by each actual inventor listing the entire inventive entity must be submitted; absence of such is a deficiency (form paragraph 2.13b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures the correct inventive entity is represented by executed declarations complying with 37 CFR 1.63 (unless other rule-permitted alternatives apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-paragraph deficiencies: Required processing fee (37 CFR 1.17(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests under 37 CFR 1.48 are deficient if they lack the required fee under 37 CFR 1.17(i) (form paragraph 2.13c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should identify this deficiency and notify the requester; fees must be paid for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-paragraph deficiencies: Written consent of assignee missing
rubrics_metrics.description: A request is deficient if it lacks the written consent of any assignee of one of the originally named inventors when such consent is required (form paragraph 2.13d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine file record for assignee indications; if none exist, requester should affirmatively state no assignee exists. See 37 CFR 3.73(b) for proving assignee authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-paragraph deficiencies: 37 CFR 3.73(b) submission missing to support assignee action
rubrics_metrics.description: A request is deficient if a 37 CFR 3.73(b) submission has not been received to support action by an assignee (form paragraph 2.13e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should require the 3.73(b) submission to establish assignee authority where assignee consent is presented or relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile inventor / inventorship overlap handling options
rubrics_metrics.description: Where it appears that an inventor to be added or deleted may be hostile and will not execute a required statement of facts, and the actual inventorship would overlap the original inventorship, applicant should consider either: (a) submission of a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 to waive that requirement if the original named inventor(s) has assigned entire right and interest and assignee consent is given, or (b) refiling the application (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.53(b) with a new oath/declaration) to eliminate need for a 1.48 request (form paragraph 2.13f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides practical options when cooperation is lacking; choice depends on assignee consent and whether refiling is feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for correction under 37 CFR 1.48(b) (deletion due to claim amendment/cancellation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If correct inventors were named in a nonprovisional and later prosecution results in amendment or cancellation of claims so that fewer of the currently named inventors are actual inventors, an amendment requesting deletion must be filed. Amendment requires: (1) a request, signed by a party set forth in §1.33(b), identifying inventor(s) to be deleted and acknowledging inventor's invention is no longer claimed; and (2) the processing fee under §1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement may be signed by applicant's registered attorney/agent who then takes responsibility for ensuring the inventor is not improperly deleted. MPEP also notes that written consent of any assignee is not required for requests filed under 37 CFR 1.48(b) (MPEP clarification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for correction under 37 CFR 1.48(c) (adding inventors for previously unclaimed subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional discloses unclaimed subject matter by persons not named as inventors when an executed declaration was first filed, the application may be amended under 37 CFR 1.48(c) to add claims and name correct inventors. Amendment requires: (1) request setting forth desired inventorship change; (2) statement from each person being added that addition is necessitated by amendment of the claims and that the inventorship error occurred without deceptive intention; (3) an oath or declaration by each actual inventor as required by §1.63 or as permitted by §§1.42, 1.43, or 1.47; (4) processing fee under §1.17(i); and (5) written consent of any assignee of the original named inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any claims added must be supported by the disclosure as filed and cannot add new matter. Use of appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 2.13.02, 2.13h) when deficiencies exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for correction under 37 CFR 1.48(d) (adding omitted inventors in provisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor's name was omitted in a provisional application through error without deceptive intent, the provisional may be amended to add the inventor. Amendment requires: (1) a request signed by a party set forth in §1.33(b) identifying inventor(s) being added and stating the error occurred without deceptive intention; and (2) the processing fee under §1.17(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement of lack of deceptive intent may be included in the request and may be signed by a registered attorney/agent. A statement of lack of deceptive intent is not required from any of the original or to-be-added inventors (MPEP clarification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for correction under 37 CFR 1.48(e) (deleting inventors in provisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person was named as an inventor in a provisional application through error without deceptive intent, an amendment may be filed deleting that person. Amendment requires: (1) a request setting forth desired inventorship change; (2) a statement by the person being deleted that the error occurred without deceptive intent; (3) the processing fee under §1.17(q); and (4) if an assignment has been executed by any original named inventors, the written consent of the assignee (see §3.73(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction in a provisional is not required to preserve benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) so long as a later nonprovisional application contains at least one inventor in common; however, correction may be desired to permit the provisional to serve as a priority basis in foreign filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of provisional inventorship errors on 35 U.S.C. 119(e) benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 119(e), a later-filed nonprovisional filed within twelve months may claim benefit of an earlier provisional so long as both applications have at least one inventor in common. An error in naming inventors in the provisional does not require correction under 1.48(d)/(e) if the nonprovisional names the correct inventorship and overlap exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correction of the provisional is nonetheless desired (e.g., to serve as a basis for foreign priority), 1.48(d)/(e) procedures apply. If correction is desired after expiration of 12 months, requests may still be filed with OIPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic inventorship correction by first-filed executed oath/declaration or cover sheet (37 CFR 1.48(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) was filed without an executed oath/declaration under §1.63, the first submission of an executed oath/declaration under §1.63 by any inventor during pendency will act to correct the earlier identification of inventorship. Similarly, if a provisional was filed without a cover sheet under §1.51(c)(1), later submission of a cover sheet will act to correct the earlier identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This automatic correction applies only if no executed oath/declaration was filed at filing. The first-filed oath/declaration determines inventorship; any subsequent oath/declaration by a different inventive entity will not be effective to change inventorship under 1.48(f)(1). Not applicable to national stage applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 371 where international inventorship differs (see 1.497(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.48(g): Office may require additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require such other information as may be deemed appropriate under the particular circumstances surrounding the correction of inventorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a catch-all allowing examiners/Office to request further evidence or documentation based on case-specific facts.
